## Purpose

`_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` splits each KV cache bucket into groups of `group_size` layers and pads the last group of each bucket. The current heuristic uses the smallest bucket as `group_size` (or the largest, if it is within 1.5x). A single-layer bucket, typically a speculative drafter layer whose spec cannot merge with the target's, drives this to `group_size = 1`, which means one KV cache group per layer, each rebuilding attention metadata every step. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash ends up with 46 groups.

This PR replaces the min / 1.5x-max heuristic:

- **Search** group sizes from `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (capped at the largest bucket) up to the largest bucket.
- **Pick** the group size that wastes the fewest worst-case bytes per request on padding layers. Each padding layer costs its spec's `max_memory_usage_bytes` at `max_model_len`, so full attention padding scales with context length, while sliding window / mamba padding stays bounded. Ties prefer fewer groups.
- **New option `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3)** trades metadata overhead (more groups) against KV capacity (more padding).
- **Equal page sizes share a group** (from tomasruizt/vllm#16, by @tomasruizt): attention layers with different head shapes but the same block size, token-slot semantics and page bytes (e.g. Qwen3.5-4B's 4×256 target and 8×128 DFlash drafter) share one KV cache group; each keeps its own spec.
- **TP-invariant planning with a KV connector:** P/D peers may run different TP sizes, which change per-rank page bytes. When `kv_transfer_config` is set, padding is costed in the pages each layer needs per request at its own page size *before* page-size unification (TP changes page bytes, not page counts), and layers are not shared by equal page size (which also depends on TP). Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash then plans 10 groups at TP 1/2/4/8 (vs 17/17/5/10 without a connector).

This subsumes the 1.5x rule (gpt-oss + eagle still pads sw 12 → 13 instead of full 13 → 24).

Grouping at `max_model_len=256k`, default `--min-kv-cache-group-layers 3`:

| Layer buckets (target + *drafter*) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash `[30 mamba, 10 full, *5 sw, 1 full*]` | gs=1, 46 groups | gs=3, 17 groups; 2 target full + 2 drafter full + 1 drafter sw padding layers |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + Eagle3 `[30 mamba, 10 full, *1 full*]` ¹ | gs=1, 41 groups | gs=5, 9 groups; 4 drafter full padding layers |
| MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash `[9 full, 39 sw, *5 sw*]` | gs=5, 11 groups; 1 full + 1 sw padding | gs=3, 18 groups; 1 drafter sw padding |
| Kimi-K3 + DSpark `[69 KDA, 24 MLA, *5 sw*]` | gs=5, 20 groups; 1 MLA + 1 KDA padding | gs=3, 33 groups; 1 drafter sw padding |
| Gemma3-27B `[52 sw, 10 full]` | gs=10, 7 groups; 8 sw padding | gs=5, 13 groups; 3 sw padding |
| gpt-oss-20b + eagle `[12 sw, 13 full]` | gs=13, 2 groups | unchanged |
| Gemma3-1B/4B/12B, Llama4-Scout, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | — | unchanged |

¹ Computed assuming the drafter's KV bytes per token equal the target's; not measured.

Behavior change: group sizes can now go below the smallest bucket, trading more groups for less (bounded) padding, e.g. Gemma3-27B 7 → 13 groups, MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash 18 groups. Whether to keep a floor at the smallest bucket is open (it gives 7 / 7 / 17 groups for Gemma3-27B / MiMo / Kimi-K3, at the cost of more bounded padding).

### Comparison with #58175

#58175 targets MiMo. On DFlash / Eagle3 it keeps main's per-layer grouping (gcd of `[10, 1]` = 1). On MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash this PR now picks the same group size (gs=3, 18 groups, no full attention padding, 1 drafter sw padding layer).

Relation to other PRs:
- #51742 ignores single-layer buckets when taking the min (gs=5 for DFlash) without bounding the resulting full attention padding.
- #49472 minimizes `padding + num_groups` in layer counts, without distinguishing full attention from bounded-memory padding (e.g. pads 3 full attention layers on Gemma3-27B).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector.py -q
```

## Test Result

**4 tests currently fail** after allowing group sizes below the smallest bucket (`test_hybrid_group_size_selection[10-52-0-3-10]`, `[9-39-5-3-9]`, `test_get_kv_cache_config_one_worker`, `test_hybrid_draft_full_attention_shapes[8-5-9]`); their expectations will be updated once the floor question above is settled. `test_kv_transfer_group_planning_is_tp_invariant` and `test_equal_page_size_sharing_disabled_with_kv_connector` cover the KV connector behavior. `test_hybrid_group_size_selection` covers the drafter (floor 2 and 3), gpt-oss + eagle, Gemma3-27B and MiMo layouts. One sub-case of `test_get_kv_cache_config_one_worker` changed expectation: at its `max_model_len=16`, a sliding window layer's worst case (2 blocks) exceeds full attention's (1 block), so padding full attention is now cheaper.

### Benchmarks

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash, 1× B300, BF16 mamba states, GSM8K, single runs, acceptance length 5.1–5.2 in all runs.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching --block-size 128 \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 --min-kv-cache-group-layers $M \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash","method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openai/gsm8k --hf-split test \
  --num-prompts max(32, 8*C) --max-concurrency C --num-warmups 2*C
```

(`--block-size 128` is needed on main too: the DFlash drafter's FLASH_ATTN backend only supports 128-token kernel blocks on B300, but the hybrid block size is aligned only to the target backend, giving 592 → `No common block size for 592`. Separate issue.)

| `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` | gs | groups | KV cache capacity | padding layers | full-context padding | 8k | 32k | 128k | 256k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (= main) | 1 | 46 | 7.42M tokens | none | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 2 | 24 | 6.42M tokens | 1 drafter full, 1 drafter sw | 4 KiB/token (+17%) | 48 MiB | 144 MiB | 528 MiB | 1.02 GiB |

| 4 | 5 | 10 | 4.80M tokens | 4 drafter full | 16 KiB/token (+67%) | 128 MiB | 512 MiB | 2 GiB | 4 GiB |

On current GDN code, default 3 trades 31% of KV capacity for 1.7% per step at c=1 and under 0.5% at c=16. With shared GDN metadata it gains nothing. On attention-only hybrids (full + sliding window; Gemma3-1B, Gemma3-27B and MiMo-V2.6-Flash + DFlash in my review above), extra groups cost nothing measurable. On faster GPUs such as B300 the per-group GDN cost is likely a larger share of the step, so the default might buy more than 1.7% there. That needs testing.

I'd make the default 1 and replace my earlier suggestion with `min(max(min(min(bucket_sizes), 3), min_group_layers), max(bucket_sizes))`. At 1 the search always includes main's group size, so capacity never drops below main. Layouts whose smallest bucket has 3 or more layers get the same widths as with my earlier suggestion, and layouts with a one-layer drafter bucket can opt in with 3. Patch below; 330 tests pass.

For drafters:
- A drafter full-attention layer with the target's page and block size can share the target's bucket instead of forming a one-layer bucket. Qwen3.5-4B + DFlash (drafter stores the same KV per token as the target), 16 GiB KV: 14 -> 5 groups, +27% KV tokens, 52.04 -> 51.91 ms/step, same greedy output. With the default-1 bound it gives 13 groups at 0.8% below main's capacity, where main uses 38 groups (offline). It does not apply when the drafter stores more KV per token than the target, as in Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash. Patch below; it stacks with the first (331 tests pass).
- The packed BLNHC layout works with #58345. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + DFlash it gives 47% more KV tokens than the default, in 5 groups, at 49.16 ms/step.

detail.body:
## Purpose

`_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` splits each KV cache bucket into groups of `group_size` layers and pads the last group of each bucket. The current heuristic uses the smallest bucket as `group_size` (or the largest, if it is within 1.5x). A single-layer bucket, typically a speculative drafter layer whose spec cannot merge with the target's, drives this to `group_size = 1`, which means one KV cache group per layer, each rebuilding attention metadata every step. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash ends up with 46 groups.

This PR replaces the min / 1.5x-max heuristic:

- **Search** group sizes from `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (capped at the largest bucket) up to the largest bucket.
- **Pick** the group size that wastes the fewest worst-case bytes per request on padding layers. Each padding layer costs its spec's `max_memory_usage_bytes` at `max_model_len`, so full attention padding scales with context length, while sliding window / mamba padding stays bounded. Ties prefer fewer groups.
- **New option `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3)** trades metadata overhead (more groups) against KV capacity (more padding).
- **Equal page sizes share a group** (from tomasruizt/vllm#16, by @tomasruizt): attention layers with different head shapes but the same block size, token-slot semantics and page bytes (e.g. Qwen3.5-4B's 4×256 target and 8×128 DFlash drafter) share one KV cache group; each keeps its own spec.
- **TP-invariant planning with a KV connector:** P/D peers may run different TP sizes, which change per-rank page bytes. When `kv_transfer_config` is set, padding is costed in the pages each layer needs per request at its own page size *before* page-size unification (TP changes page bytes, not page counts), and layers are not shared by equal page size (which also depends on TP). Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash then plans 10 groups at TP 1/2/4/8 (vs 17/17/5/10 without a connector).

This subsumes the 1.5x rule (gpt-oss + eagle still pads sw 12 → 13 instead of full 13 → 24).

Grouping at `max_model_len=256k`, default `--min-kv-cache-group-layers 3`:

| Layer buckets (target + *drafter*) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash `[30 mamba, 10 full, *5 sw, 1 full*]` | gs=1, 46 groups | gs=3, 17 groups; 2 target full + 2 drafter full + 1 drafter sw padding layers |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + Eagle3 `[30 mamba, 10 full, *1 full*]` ¹ | gs=1, 41 groups | gs=5, 9 groups; 4 drafter full padding layers |
| MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash `[9 full, 39 sw, *5 sw*]` | gs=5, 11 groups; 1 full + 1 sw padding | gs=3, 18 groups; 1 drafter sw padding |
| Kimi-K3 + DSpark `[69 KDA, 24 MLA, *5 sw*]` | gs=5, 20 groups; 1 MLA + 1 KDA padding | gs=3, 33 groups; 1 drafter sw padding |
| Gemma3-27B `[52 sw, 10 full]` | gs=10, 7 groups; 8 sw padding | gs=5, 13 groups; 3 sw padding |
| gpt-oss-20b + eagle `[12 sw, 13 full]` | gs=13, 2 groups | unchanged |
| Gemma3-1B/4B/12B, Llama4-Scout, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | — | unchanged |

¹ Computed assuming the drafter's KV bytes per token equal the target's; not measured.

Behavior change: group sizes can now go below the smallest bucket, trading more groups for less (bounded) padding, e.g. Gemma3-27B 7 → 13 groups, MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash 18 groups. Whether to keep a floor at the smallest bucket is open (it gives 7 / 7 / 17 groups for Gemma3-27B / MiMo / Kimi-K3, at the cost of more bounded padding).

### Comparison with #58175

#58175 targets MiMo. On DFlash / Eagle3 it keeps main's per-layer grouping (gcd of `[10, 1]` = 1). On MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash this PR now picks the same group size (gs=3, 18 groups, no full attention padding, 1 drafter sw padding layer).

Relation to other PRs:
- #51742 ignores single-layer buckets when taking the min (gs=5 for DFlash) without bounding the resulting full attention padding.
- #49472 minimizes `padding + num_groups` in layer counts, without distinguishing full attention from bounded-memory padding (e.g. pads 3 full attention layers on Gemma3-27B).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector.py -q
```

## Test Result

**4 tests currently fail** after allowing group sizes below the smallest bucket (`test_hybrid_group_size_selection[10-52-0-3-10]`, `[9-39-5-3-9]`, `test_get_kv_cache_config_one_worker`, `test_hybrid_draft_full_attention_shapes[8-5-9]`); their expectations will be updated once the floor question above is settled. `test_kv_transfer_group_planning_is_tp_invariant` and `test_equal_page_size_sharing_disabled_with_kv_connector` cover the KV connector behavior. `test_hybrid_group_size_selection` covers the drafter (floor 2 and 3), gpt-oss + eagle, Gemma3-27B and MiMo layouts. One sub-case of `test_get_kv_cache_config_one_worker` changed expectation: at its `max_model_len=16`, a sliding window layer's worst case (2 blocks) exceeds full attention's (1 block), so padding full attention is now cheaper.

### Benchmarks

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash, 1× B300, BF16 mamba states, GSM8K, single runs, acceptance length 5.1–5.2 in all runs.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching --block-size 128 \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 --min-kv-cache-group-layers $M \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash","method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openai/gsm8k --hf-split test \
  --num-prompts max(32, 8*C) --max-concurrency C --num-warmups 2*C
```

(`--block-size 128` is needed on main too: the DFlash drafter's FLASH_ATTN backend only supports 128-token kernel blocks on B300, but the hybrid block size is aligned only to the target backend, giving 592 → `No common block size for 592`. Separate issue.)

Left: this PR. Right: this PR + #52297 (GDN metadata, orthogonal). `--min-kv-cache-group-layers 1` reproduces main's grouping (46 groups).

![min-kv-cache-group-layers sweep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/af4013a3827d250b266c6e48b1fc124880523780/pareto_min_layers.png)

Grouping and padding cost per request vs. context length. Target full attention is 2 KiB/token/layer (2 KV heads × 256); drafter layers are 4 KiB/token/layer (8 KV heads × 128). For reference, the unpadded full attention KV is 24 KiB/token (10 target + 1 drafter layer).

| `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` | gs | groups | KV cache capacity | padding layers | full-context padding | 8k | 32k | 128k | 256k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (= main) | 1 | 46 | 7.42M tokens | none | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 2 | 24 | 6.42M tokens | 1 drafter full, 1 drafter sw | 4 KiB/token (+17%) | 48 MiB | 144 MiB | 528 MiB | 1.02 GiB |
| 3 (default) | 3 | 17 | 5.19M tokens | 2 target full, 2 drafter full, 1 drafter sw | 12 KiB/token (+50%) | 112 MiB | 400 MiB | 1.52 GiB | 3.02 GiB |
| 4 | 5 | 10 | 4.80M tokens | 4 drafter full | 16 KiB/token (+67%) | 128 MiB | 512 MiB | 2 GiB | 4 GiB |

The sliding window padding layer adds a bounded ~16 MiB (4096-token window × 4 KiB), included above. The measured KV cache capacity drops (−13.5% / −30% / −35%) track the full-context overhead.
